info.text:
An eviction case can follow you for 7 years.
Landlords filed 1.23 million eviction cases in 2025 across the areas Princeton's Eviction Lab tracks.
The usual path (rules vary by state): late fee, pay-or-quit notice (example: 3 days in California, 14 in New York), lawsuit, judgment, removal by a sheriff or marshal.
Credit reports generally leave evictions off, but unpaid rent sent to collections can stay up to 7 years. Tenant screening reports can list eviction cases for up to 7 years (CFPB).
In 2023, TransUnion agreed to pay $15 million to settle FTC and CFPB allegations it misreported eviction records. Local legal aid or 211 can point you to help.
Sources: Eviction Lab (Apr 2026), CFPB, FTC, Experian, CA Attorney General, NY CourtHelp.
News and education, not financial advice.
